## Reporting rules

- Each seat reads the issue and relevant latest comments before starting an assignment.
- A seat may work only on its assigned task and paths, using a separate branch/worktree from the assigned base SHA. A report does not reserve files or authorize work; a coordinator assignment does.
- The coordinator manages pushes, Draft PRs and integration. Worker seats deliver commits plus a Git bundle when their runtime is separate, unless their task explicitly grants push permission.
- Append reports as comments. Do not overwrite other seats' reports or the coordinator register. Corrections reference the earlier report ID.
- Reports bind results to an exact SHA and environment. Distinguish worker-reported results from independently verified results. CI success, acceptance and deployment are separate facts.
- Do not store credentials, customer records, raw logs, private oversight notes or local-only artifact links. Use approved GitHub links or an actual transferred attachment; never assume filesystems are shared.
- Do not repeat successful tests merely to populate this register.
- Before posting, check the latest comments for the same report ID. Reconcile uncertain delivery before retrying. This is a manual deduplication rule, not an atomic API guarantee.
- If a seat lacks GitHub write permission, return the report in chat for the coordinator to post. Do not change permissions.


Unknown fields must be marked unknown with a reason. A seat must not mark itself accepted, closed, merged or released based only on its own tests. Those decisions belong to the designated reviewer/coordinator and require the applicable authorization.

# AI CLI Tools Community Digest 2026-11-11 > Generated: 2026-11-11 01:11 UTC | Tools covered: 7 - [Claude Code](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code) - [OpenAI Codex](https://github​.com/openai/codex) - [Gemini CLI](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) - [GitHub Copilot CLI](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli) - [OpenCode](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode) - [Pi](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi) - [Qwen Code](https://github​.com/QwenLM/qwen-code) - [Claude Code Skills](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills) --- ## Cross-Tool Comparison # Cross-Tool Comparison Report: AI CLI Developer Tools **Date: 2026-11-11** | Source: Community digests from GitHub activity --- ## 1. Ecosystem Overview The AI CLI tools landscape on 2026-11-11 shows a maturing ecosystem in which **reliability and trust** have replaced raw capability as the dominant community concern. Across seven major tools, release velocity is modest (mostly patch-level), but issue trackers are busy — with Windows platform regressions, MCP integration fragility, and agent-permission/trust failures forming the loudest cross-cutting clusters. A clear platform divide persists: Windows and Linux/Wayland users repeatedly report second-class experiences, while macOS-adjacent workflows dominate. Meanwhile, a shared architectural pivot is underway — several tools are hardening subagent execution semantics, session durability, and sandbox/credential isolation, suggesting the industry is consolidating around agentic workflows rather than expanding feature surface area. --- ## 2. Activity Comparison | Tool | Issues (updated today) | PRs (updated today) | Discussions | Release Status | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Claude Code** | ~15+ (10 detailed) | 1 (closed) | N/A (not provided) | v2.1.322 — minor (Vertex fast-mode) | | **OpenAI Codex** | ~13 (10 detailed + 3 HM) | 10 (bot-authored, CLOSED) | 4 (Show & Tell / General) | rust-v0.167.1 patch; rust-v0.169.0-alpha.9 | | **Gemini CLI** | 10 detailed | 10 | N/A (not provided) | v0.69.0-preview.0; v0.68.0 (docs-only) | | **GitHub Copilot CLI** | 10 detailed | 1 (open) | N/A | v1.0.110-1; v1.0.110-0 | | **OpenCode** | 10 detailed | 10 + 3 notable | N/A | v2.2.7 (Copilot Auto routing) | | **Pi** | 10 detailed | 10 + ~5 notable | 1 (Ideas) | v1.5.2 (orphan session forking) | | **Qwen Code** | 10 detailed | 10 | N/A (not provided) | v0.27.2; v0.27.2-preview.0; SDK TS v0.1.32 | **Notes:** - Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Copilot CLI show sparse PR activity in the reporting window; Codex's PRs are bot-authored and marked CLOSED (likely internal merge/projection artifacts). - Discussions data was not supplied for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, or Qwen Code — marked **N/A**, not "inactive." - All seven tools shipped at least one release; only OpenCode (Copilot Auto routing), Pi (orphan session forking), and Gemini CLI (`/stats heatmap`) shipped user-visible features. --- ## 3. Shared Feature Directions Several requirements recur across **three or more** tool communities, indicating converging user expectations: ### 3.1 Agent Trust, Permissions & Control - **Claude Code**: auto-mode classifier overriding explicit allow rules (#100221); orchestrator ignoring standing instructions (#108601) - **OpenCode**: plan mode broken (#60250); agent acting after STOP (#63216); deny rules lacking explanatory messages (#63075) - **Gemini CLI**: destructive `git reset --force` behavior (#22672); settings.json overrides ignored (#22267) - **Qwen Code**: AUTO classifier fed already-executed calls (#16496); permission approval never rendering (#16425) - **Codex**: "Always allow" not overriding denials (#49453); Full access vanishing mid-chat (#60058) **Shared need:** Deterministic, inspectable permission models where user intent is honored predictably. ### 3.2 MCP Integration Maturity - **Claude Code**: auth/token cluster (#108783, #108794, #108677, #103809) - **Copilot CLI**: tool exposure (#191), orphaned processes (#4392/#4461), protocol-era mismatch (#4888), Entra silent sign-in (#5402) - **Gemini CLI**: >128 tools 400 error (#24246) - **Codex**: browser/permission integration regressions **Shared need:** First-class MCP auth UX, lifecycle management, and tool scoping. ### 3.3 Windows Platform Parity - **Claude Code**: 12s image-paste freeze (#108217), console spam (#99851), sidebar state loss (#104476) - **Codex**: VS Code extension init failure (#56655), project loss (#59895), AbsolutePathBuf (#59855) - **Copilot CLI**: NumLock regression (#5171), PowerShell parent kill (#5404), credential storage - **OpenCode**: console flashing (#52266), stale file trees (#52941) **Shared need:** Windows treated as a first-class target, not a port. ### 3.4 Usage & Cost Visibility - **Claude Code**: inline usage/reset/duration (#108488) - **Codex**: always-visible remaining usage (#25561) - **Gemini CLI**: `/stats heatmap` shipped in v0.69.0-preview.0 - **Copilot CLI**: credit-consumption concern on failed responses (#5408) **Shared need:** Real-time token/quota telemetry to support budgeting. ### 3.5 Remote / Headless Parity - **Codex**: device-code TUI auth (#60662), Cloud model selection (#60651), Android Remote nav (#42489) - **Copilot CLI**: remote environment hosting (#5283), Connectors in `--acp` (#5397) - **OpenCode**: session-scoped MCP (#63213), org remote policy (#63139) **Shared need:** Full workflow parity without requiring a desktop session. ### 3.6 Subagent Reliability - **Gemini CLI**: false success after MAX_TURNS (#22323), hangs (#21409), ignored settings (#22267) - **OpenCode**: stacked PRs #63209/#63210/#63223 reworking subagent semantics - **Qwen Code**: subagent context blow-up (#15660), teammate→leader delivery (#15738) **Shared need:** Predictable, observable, and resource-bounded delegation. --- ## 4. Differentiation Analysis | Dimension | Claude Code | OpenAI Codex | Gemini CLI | Copilot CLI | OpenCode | Pi | Qwen Code | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Primary focus** | Enterprise agentic coding + MCP depth | Broad multi-surface (CLI/VS Code/Desktop/Cloud/Mobile) | Gemini-native agent + browser automation | GitHub-integrated agent + sandbox | Open-source TUI + plugin ecosystem | Session/state durability + provider breadth | Managed Agent + Web Shell channels | | **Target user** | Professional devs, enterprises | Pro/Plus consumer + enterprise mix | Gemini 3 users, Linux/macOS devs | GitHub-centric teams | Plugin devs, power users | Extension authors, multi-provider users | Multi-channel / team workflows | | **Technical bets** | Remote Control, coordinator/device-mode, Vertex | Computer Use, Browser Use, signer service | AST-aware tooling, unified agent loop | Sandboxed credential handling, ACP | Plugin HTTP hooks, pipe-mode daemon | Chord storage migration, Redux-style state | Unified agent loop, GraphQL batching | | **Weakest surface** | Remote Control registration, MCP auth | Windows desktop | Subagent reliability | MCP + Windows | Windows desktop | Cache warming, type-safety | CI flakiness, safety classifier | | **Release cadence** | Quiet patch days | Rapid alpha cadence | Preview + stable parallel | Steady patch line | Feature-rich patches | Migration-heavy | Fast SDK + CLI coupling | **Notable differentiation:** - **Claude Code** leans hardest into MCP as a first-class surface — and pays the price with the most visible MCP auth cluster. - **Codex** is the only tool with meaningful **Computer Use / Browser Use** integration, and the only one shipping a **macOS signer service** — indicating supply-chain maturity focus. - **OpenCode** is the most architecturally active: stacked subagent PRs and a structural Windows fix (pipe-mode daemon, #63196) suggest an engineering-led roadmap. - **Pi** is unusual in optimizing for **provider breadth and session portability** (Chord storage, orphan session forking, Azure Entra, LM Studio) — a "multi-model, multi-backend" positioning. - **Qwen Code** is the only tool where **CI flakiness dominates the top of the issue tracker** (#14724 with 292 comments), and the only one with a **Channel ecosystem** (WeChat/QQ/Email) — a distinctively China-market-oriented integration strategy. - **Copilot CLI** is the only tool with a **sandbox credential-masking** model — and a matching security-relevant bug (#5388). --- ## 5. Community Momentum & Maturity ### Highest engagement (by comment/upvote volume) 1. **OpenAI Codex** — #56655 (74c, 85👍) and #59895 (52c) top the entire dataset. Windows VS Code breakage has galvanized the community. 2. **Qwen Code** — #14724 (292c) is the single most-commented item across all tools, though this is a CI tracking issue, not a user-facing bug. 3. **Claude Code** — #100377 (18c), #106167 (16c), #102952 (12c, 18👍) show broad, diverse engagement. 4. **OpenCode** — #55446 (20c, 13👍) and a coherent Windows regression cluster indicate an active, opinionated user base. 5. **Copilot CLI** — #4438 (17c, 20👍) and #191 (15c, 15👍) show high signal-to-noise on MCP and skill-invocation issues. ### Rapid iterators (feature-level movement today) - **OpenCode** — shipped Copilot Auto routing; 10 PRs incl. 3 stacked subagent reworks and a structural Windows fix. - **Pi** — v1.5.2 feature + heavy Chord migration PR wave (#11951, #12002, #12011, #11990). - **Qwen Code** — CLI + SDK releases same day; Managed Agent ledger hardening. - **Gemini CLI** — `/stats heatmap` + template `$` fix; active security PRs (#30171, #30095). ### Slower cadence but mature - **Claude Code** — single patch release; but the issue tracker shows deep, well-documented reports (e.g., #108601 written by the session itself). - **Copilot CLI** — steady v1.0.110 line; minimal PR activity but substantive issue detail. ### Maturity signals - **Gemini CLI** and **Qwen Code** both show **automated CI-failure tracking issues** — a sign of engineering process maturity (and pain). - **Codex** and **OpenCode** show **bot-authored PRs** — evidence of internal CI/projection workflows. - **Pi** and **OpenCode** show **stacked PR series** — mature review discipline. --- ## 6. Trend Signals ### 6.1 The trust gap is the #1 industry-wide risk Across Claude Code, OpenCode, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex, the most damaging complaints are not missing features but **violated user intent**: agents acting after STOP, classifiers overriding explicit allow rules, plan mode executing instead of planning, and settings being silently ignored. **Recommendation for decision-makers:** evaluate tools on their permission-model auditability, not on agent capability benchmarks. ### 6.2 MCP is shipping faster than its auth ergonomics Every tool that touches MCP — Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, Codex — has an active MCP auth/lifecycle bug cluster. The pattern (token rotation, single-tenant Entra, OAuth callback ports, tool-count limits) is consistent enough to suggest an **industry-wide gap in MCP client maturity**. **Recommendation:** budget for MCP integration maintenance; prefer tools with visible MCP auth UX roadmaps (Copilot CLI's #5410 and #5391 are directional). ### 6.3 Windows is the ecosystem's structural debt Four of seven tools have Windows-specific clusters of comparable severity. This is not a single vendor's problem — it reflects the **CI/CD and dev-tooling ecosystem's macOS/Linux bias**. **Recommendation:** Windows-based teams should pilot-test all candidate tools before standardizing. ### 6.4 Session durability and state migration is the next frontier Pi's Chord migration wave, OpenCode's subagent rework, Qwen Code's durable `/loop` wakeups, and Claude Code's compaction-related instruction drift all point to a shared realization: **agent sessions are becoming long-lived stateful entities** that need database-grade storage semantics. **Recommendation:** watch Pi's Chord architecture and OpenCode's `create_pipe`/pipe-mode work as leading indicators. ### 6.5 Subagent execution semantics are being standardized Three tools independently converged on "always-background, report-on-idle" subagent models (OpenCode's PR stack, Gemini's MAX_TURNS fix-in-flight, Qwen's teammate delivery). This suggests a **de facto industry pattern** for delegation is emerging. **Recommendation:** for extension authors, target background-first subagent APIs. ### 6.6 Cost visibility is becoming table stakes Gemini CLI shipped `/stats heatmap`; Claude Code and Codex both have active requests; Copilot CLI's #5408 (1,002.5 credits on failed responses) shows the cost of opacity. **Recommendation:** treat usage telemetry as a procurement requirement, not a nice-to-have. ### 6.7 Platform-specific bets reveal strategic positioning - **Qwen Code's** WeChat/QQ/Email channels target the China enterprise messaging stack. - **Codex's** Computer Use + signer service targets macOS-first prosumer workflows. - **Pi's** Azure Entra + LM Studio + Cloudflare breadth targets the multi-cloud/multi-provider enterprise. - **Copilot CLI's** credential masking targets regulated/GHE environments. **Recommendation:** match tool selection to your deployment geography, cloud posture, and compliance envelope — the ecosystem is diverging along these axes. --- *Report compiled from community digests dated 2026-11-11. Comment/upvote counts are point-in-time. Where source data omitted a section (e.g., Discussions for most tools), that is noted as N/A rather than inferred.* --- ## Per-Tool Reports

Today's Highlights A quiet release day: v2.1.322 ships only a Vertex-specific fast-mode improvement, falling back to standard speed gracefully. The issue tracker, however, is busy — Remote Control session registration failures (#100377, #106900, #108529) are clearly a cluster regression affecting macOS and Linux users, and a cluster of MCP auth/token bugs (#108783, #108794, #108677) points to persistent friction in the MCP integration surface. Windows TUI and desktop performance issues (#108217, #99851) also remain unaddressed. ## 2. Releases **v2.1.322** — Minor update. - Added fast mode on Vertex AI in the `global`, `us`, and `eu` regions, with automatic fallback to standard speed if Vertex rejects the fast-mode request. No other changes. - Link: [anthropics/claude-code releases](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases) ## 3. Hot Issues 1. **[#100377](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/100377)** (18 comments) — Remote Control: Project threads on macOS fail with CCR v2 worker registration 400, while self-started sessions on the same server register fine. Highest-engagement issue today; clearly a regression in the coordinator/device-mode path. No maintainer response visible yet despite 18 comments. 2. **[#106167](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/106167)** (16 comments, 👍10) — Server-delivered "games" instruction blocks interfere with professional development work. Notable for its high upvote count and the unusual nature of the complaint — model-side instruction injection affecting real workloads. 3. **[#107232](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/107232)** (15 comments) — Claude Code still cannot handle API requests longer than 5 minutes on Linux. A longstanding, recurring complaint; the "still an issue" framing suggests prior reports were closed without a fix. 4. **[#102952](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/102952)** (12 comments, 👍18) — Feature request to bring back the glowing code-glyph ripple background on the desktop home screen. Highest upvote count among open issues today; a purely aesthetic regression that the community clearly noticed. 5. **[#105334](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/105334)** (6 comments, 👍7) — Desktop app declines MCP elicitation requests without showing them, while still advertising elicitation support. A correctness bug with security-adjacent implications for MCP server authors. 6. **[#108601](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/108601)** (5 comments) — Long-running orchestrator sessions repeatedly violate explicit standing instructions across Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1, including across compactions. Written by the session itself from its own transcript — an unusually well-documented agent-alignment complaint. 7. **[#108217](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/108217)** (5 comments) — Windows Alt+V image paste blocks the event loop for ~12s, freezing the TUI. Performance regression with concrete CPU measurements. 8. **[#104476](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/104476)** (5 comments) — Windows desktop: chats disappear from sidebar groups until a new message is sent. Tagged `invalid` but still attracting comments, suggesting a UX or state-management rough edge. 9. **[#99851](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/99851)** (4 comments) — Windows: every prompt spawns 3–5 `git.exe` processes that each open a visible console window. Long-running annoyance for Windows users launching `claude` as a child process. 10. **[#100221](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/100221)** (1 comment) — Auto-mode classifier hard-denies commands explicitly allowed by user permission rules, with no approval path. Low comment count but high severity: a permissions-model escape hatch gap. ## 4. Key PR Progress Only one PR was updated in the last 24 hours: 1. **[#74722](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/74722)** [CLOSED] — `feat(commit-commands): support Conventional Branch naming in /commit-push-pr`. Adds an optional `conventional` argument to `/commit-push-pr` that names new branches per Conventional Branch 1.0.0 (`/`), inferring the type from the diff. Closed after ~4 months; the outcome (merged vs. rejected) is not reflected in the supplied data. Worth watching if you rely on the commit-commands workflow. *Note: with only one PR in the update window, there is no meaningful "top 10" — the remainder of this section is omitted rather than padded.* ## 5. Hot Discussions No Discussion data was provided for this window. Section omitted. ## 6. Feature Request Trends Distilled from today's Issues: - **Desktop UI polish and personalization** — restoring the glowing code-glyph ripple background (#102952, 👍18), custom dictation vocabulary (#108937), and desktop-specific visual regressions are a recurring theme. Users treat the desktop app as a first-class product and expect it to be maintained as such. - **Cost and session visibility** — showing usage, reset time, and task duration snapshots inline in conversations (#108488). A persistent ask from heavy users who need to budget tokens. - **TUI/native affordances** — flag emojis as reactions (#107665) and other small quality-of-life terminal improvements. - **MCP auth UX** — an Authenticate button in the VS Code MCP panel (#108783) and custom-word support imply users want first-class UI for configuration surfaces that are currently CLI- or config-file-driven. - **Cross-platform parity** — repeated requests to bring macOS-only behaviors (e.g., Vertex fast mode scope, Windows console suppression) to parity across platforms. ## 7. Developer Pain Points Recurring frustrations visible across today's issue set: - **Remote Control / CCR v2 registration is unreliable.** Three separate issues (#100377, #106900, #108529) describe 400 errors, unrecoverable sessions after host reboot, and Project-thread-specific failures. This is the single most coherent bug cluster in the tracker right now. - **MCP authentication and token lifecycle is fragile.** Rotating refresh tokens get revoked when multiple sessions share a sign-in (#108794), MCP widgets lose `structuredContent` in the Desktop Code tab (#103809), optional-auth HTTP servers can't be signed into from VS Code (#108783), and Gmail's remote MCP server authenticates but then fails on `tools/list` (#108677). MCP is shipping faster than its auth ergonomics can keep up. - **Long-running requests and sessions break.** The >5-minute API request ceiling (#107232) and the stop-hook loop on unmeetable `/goal` conditions (#106573) both hit users running long autonomous tasks — exactly the workflow Claude Code is marketed for. - **Windows remains a second-class citizen.** Visible console windows per `git.exe` spawn (#99851), 12-second TUI freezes on image paste (#108217), and chats vanishing from sidebar groups (#104476) accumulate into a poor daily experience. - **Permission and instruction authority is unclear.** The auto-mode classifier overriding explicit user allow rules (#100221) and orchestrator sessions ignoring written standing instructions (#108601) both point to a trust gap: users cannot reliably predict when their explicit configuration will be honored. - **Stale-close friction.** Several issues (#92457, #92247, #92446, #92386) were closed as `stale` rather than fixed, including a documented off-by-one in skill argument substitution — contributing to the "still an issue" tone in newer reports. --- *Generated from GitHub data for 2026-11-11. Stacked on #63209. 2. **[#63209 — Report subagent results on every idle](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63209)** (jlongster) — Children now report to the parent each time they go idle, not just at one-shot job completion — covers directly-typed, re-prompted, and self-woken children. 3. **[#63223 — Remove unused foreground path from SubagentJob](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63223)** (jlongster) — Cleanup stacked on #63210; deletes dead code after all callers passed `{ background: true }`. 4. **[#62820 — Experimental model HTTP hooks for plugins](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62820)** (rekram1-node) — Extends plugin HTTP hooks beyond Session requests to cover `generate` text/image/decision calls, unblocking use cases like provider client certificates (#62096). 5. **[#63196 — Pipe mode on Windows for the process daemon](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63196)** (jlongster) — Adds `create_pipe`: commands with no console (`CREATE_NO_WINDOW`), stdin from `NUL`. Likely the structural fix for the console-flashing family of issues. 6. **[#63200 — Run LM Studio decision models](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63200)** (rekram1-node) — Follow-up enabling LM Studio decision models, continuing the local-model integration line (#56214, #63198). 7. **[#63208 — Stop freezing desktop main process during shell env probe](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63208)** (rekram1-node) — Replaces blocking `spawnSync` of `$SHELL -il -c "env -0"` (up to 5s startup freeze) with async probing. (Closed, merged-track.) 8. **[#63222 — `opencode api` waits for plugins before sending](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63222)** (ssskay) — Fixes plugin-init race in the `api` command, matching existing `waitForPlugins` behavior in `models` and `debug agents`. 9. **[#63220 — Keep pairing QR code scannable in every theme](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63220)** (ssskay) — Draws QR black-on-white under all themes so scanners that reject inverted codes (e.g. Android) can pair. Closes #63150. 10. **[#61299 — @-mention files outside the project directory](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61299)** (bruno303) — Ports the V1 external-file mention feature to V2 TUI, per maintainer request to reopen against V2 (#16463/#16464). *Also notable:* [#63213](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63213) (session-scoped client MCP connections), [#63139](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63139) (`remote.use` org policy to disable remote access), [#63207](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63207) (TUI transcript verbosity defaults to `low`). --- ## Feature Request Trends 1. **Desktop organization & navigation** — Project-grouped sidebars (#55446, 👍13), keyboard-shortcut help overlay (#63190), and sidebar row parity between Recent and side tabs (#63211). The desktop shell is the most feature-hungry surface. 2. **Context/transcript editing** — Long-running calls to delete or modify messages in the thread (#7712, 👍13; #7034, 👍4), driven by dead-end contexts. Consistently high upvote counts for an unshipped capability. 3. **Extensible permissions and agent control** — Passing reasons/alternatives through deny rules (#63075), and plugin APIs to steer or rewrite conversation threads (#7034). 4. **Remote & multi-session workflows** — Session-scoped MCP connections (#63213), org-level remote-access policy (#63139), and fixing devcontainer multi-instance collisions (#50329). 5. **Platform & local-model breadth** — Android 17 local-network permission (#62934), iOS dictation language support (#56973), and expanded LM Studio integration (#63200). --- ## Developer Pain Points - **Windows desktop is the clear weak spot.** Phantom console windows on spawned processes (#52266, #62988), stale Review-pane file trees (#52941, #63214), and a background service that steals keyboard focus (every ~2s in #62988) form a cluster of visible, disruptive regressions. Notably, the platform fix (pipe mode, #63196) and the diagnostics are now converging. - **Agent control and trust remain contested.** Plan mode failing to stay in plan (#60250) and an agent acting after an explicit STOP (#63216) represent the most serious class of complaints — they erode confidence in the plan/permission model. - **Entitlement and billing friction.** Active subscriptions with 0% usage returning "insufficient funds" (#51424), ChatGPT subscription-sharing limit false positives (#62529), and repeated "no quota despite no usage" reports (#62996) suggest quota-accounting mismatches that are painful because they're opaque to users. - **Silent failure modes.** Turns settling as "succeeded" with zero content (#63171), interrupted tools losing partial results (#39565), and stale TLS/keep-alive reuse on Windows (#59786) all share a theme: failures that leave no useful trace, making debugging hard. - **Data integrity fears.** The 2.2.5→2.2.6 total session loss (#62659), even with few comments, is the kind of incident that damages trust disproportionately and warrants a prominent postmortem. - **Hardware/runtime compatibility cliffs.** The SSE4.2 requirement (#59461) locks out older CPUs entirely with a bare Error 134 — no graceful degradation path. --- *Generated from github.com/anomalyco/opencode activity for 2026-11-11. - Один законченный продуктовый пакет в работе на направление. Один основной исполнитель сохраняет пакет от source до разрешённого installed release; ручной диалог и задание одного направления не являются двумя владельцами. - Source разных направлений может идти параллельно при непересекающихся claims. В каждом claim: эффект, точные paths/base/head, операция, необходимые gates, следующий шаг и владелец. - Не требовать нового «давай дальше» для уже разрешённых действий. Не останавливать зелёный разрешённый пакет на PR; доводить публикацию и передачу. Исходные разрешения source/push/PR/merge/deploy/внешних записей не расширяются.
- Проверки — по изменённому риску и действующим обязательным current-head gates. Сохранять доказательства и разрешённый reuse; не повторять неизменённые полные CI/browser baselines ради статуса. Реализовано / CI / опубликовано / installed / natural / physical фиксируются раздельно.
- Пользователь обсуждает профильную работу в соответствующем существующем диалоге; здесь — общие решения и зависимости. Одна задача не дублируется во всех диалогах. Источник исполняемого состояния — свежие #55/PR/claims/receipts, а не память другого чата.

Историческое основание уже выполненных1089/1090/1092/1094, не текущая команда реализации: разбор исходников на `f31769918fb0aadfcc09f9bb2a305111a9c58fc7`: API detail продвигает read-marker после гидратации последней порции до подтверждения показа браузером; text send guard подавляет одинаковый текст в пределах 3 секунд; история обнаруживает разрыв с ручной дозагрузкой. Это подтверждённые границы кода и основания для следующего среза, не доказанные новые production-инциденты. Ограничение DOM и скрытые панели пока гипотезы производительности.

Ориентиры: [Telegram visible-read observer](https://github.com/Ajaxy/telegram-tt/blob/f67a40879a7d78c2683ec5a296cf55bc22417d56/src/components/middle/hooks/useMessageObservers.ts), [Telegram scroll anchoring](https://github.com/Ajaxy/telegram-tt/blob/f67a40879a7d78c2683ec5a296cf55bc22417d56/src/components/middle/MessageList.tsx), [Chatwoot reconnect](https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/blob/develop/app/javascript/dashboard/helper/ReconnectService.js), [EspoCRM hidden panel fetch](https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm/blob/master/client/src/views/stream/panel.js). Переносить проверенные правила поведения в нашу архитектуру с учётом лицензий конкретных файлов. Общую прочитанность Chatwoot не переносить поверх нашей персональной модели.

## Границы завершения

- #928/#929 целиком не закрыты; техническая публикация не равна подтверждённой повседневной работе менеджера.
- Рабочий профиль ответов остаётся GPT-6.1 Sol / reasoning low / Standard (default). Старые упоминания Fast не являются распоряжением менять модель или конфигурацию.
- Согласованная интеграция существующих напоминаний не возобновляет весь CRM/#938. Дополнение владельца22.10 разрешает readonly аналитику/воронку; новые сделки, изменение стадий и CRM-автоматизация остаются вне пакета.
- Не менять routing, смены, отправку лидов, Метрику, source attribution, расписания или соседние проекты; автоматические отправки туристам не добавлять.

## 1. Program objective

Move from the historical custom-infrastructure / manual-exchange-click compromise to:

```text
PROJECT-OWNED VERSIONED STRATEGY / RESEARCH
+
MATURE NAUTILUS TRADING INFRASTRUCTURE
+
```

while minimizing:

- real-money risk;
- framework lock-in;
- upgrade cost;
- duplicated commodity infrastructure;
- strategy regression;
- user relay / repeated rebuild work.

Autonomous execution is not part of the current delivery target.

---

## 2. Critical distinction — Infrastructure version and Strategy version are separate axes

```text
INFRASTRUCTURE_VERSION != STRATEGY_VERSION
```

Two independent promotion tracks exist:

```text
TRACK F — FRAMEWORK / INFRASTRUCTURE
Nautilus fit -> adoption -> Shadow runtime -> approval plumbing -> Testnet -> production version qualification

TRACK S — STRATEGY / EDGE
Three Setup Champion -> latest research -> retrospective/OOS -> Forward Shadow -> Strategy Promotion
```

They intentionally converge only before real-capital Human-approved execution.

Permanent regression-isolation rule:

```text
WHEN_NAUTILUS_VERSION_CHANGES => FREEZE_STRATEGY_ECONOMICS
WHEN_STRATEGY_VERSION_CHANGES => FREEZE_NAUTILUS_INFRASTRUCTURE_VERSION
```

Do not combine a framework breaking-change migration and a Strategy economics change into one acceptance claim.

---

**YES.**

The development/integration path may begin with the current stable Three Setup Champion because it provides a known reference Strategy for infrastructure equivalence and regression testing.

The final Human-approved execution Strategy is **not required to remain that Champion forever**.

```text

-> LATEST E5-ELIGIBLE FROZEN STRATEGY/POLICY/PARAMETER VERSION
-> HUMAN-APPROVED EXECUTION
```

If no Challenger reaches promotion quality by the execution gate, use the stable Champion. Do not delay indefinitely or promote weak evidence merely because a newer idea exists.

If a Challenger reaches promotion quality in time, the final launch may use that newer promoted Strategy.
